findings.text: Per-vCPU virtualized interrupt preparation provides an operation that readies remapping linkage and its synchronization, completes without further work when acceleration is disabled or no kernel interrupt chip is present, and otherwise establishes backing storage and adopts a flat destination organization as the initial value.

Posted-interrupt routing provides an update contract taking host identity, guest identity, an optional target and a vector. It guarantees prior linkage is dropped, programs new affinity with guest tagging and current activity state when a target exists and records opaque remapping state on success, clears programming when no target exists, and reverts to legacy handling with an I/O failure indication when required remapping state is absent.

Remapping linkage is guarded by a per-vCPU raw spinlock with interrupt state preserved. Detachment acquires it around list removal, and affinity programming holds it across host CPU selection and linkage insertion to prevent concurrent schedule, migration or reprogramming from observing stale placement.

Per-vCPU remapping state consists of a list head for active associations plus its lock, where each association links a kernel interrupt object node and retains an opaque handle supplied by the remapping layer for later affinity maintenance, iterated to propagate CPU and wake-policy changes.

Virtualized interrupt CPU actions use a small flag set where activation and deactivation share one toggle bit because refresh only occurs while running, running transitions carry no distinct value because blocking transitions subsume them, and entering blocking carries a separate bit that requests wake-via-log programming.

Affinity propagation requires the remapping lock already held and does nothing when no associations exist. Processor load and unload paths require preemption disabled and hold that lock while updating both cached and shared placement entries and notifying the remapping layer, ensuring concurrent association changes see consistent placement.

Placement state comprises a per-vCPU cached entry and a per-VM shared table indexed by vCPU identifier. Each entry conveys a host identifier, a running indication and a synthetic log request used only in the cached copy. Updates validate identifier width and table bounds, preserve the host identifier across unload for containment, and suppress the running indication in the shared copy when IPI virtualization is disabled.

Load, unload, blocking and unblocking form a lifecycle where load is skipped while blocking with placement deferred to wake, unload clears running while preserving placement and optionally records a log request when blocking, blocking forces unload before sleep to quiesce doorbells and enable wake detection, and unblocking reloads on the current processor. Unload distinguishes preemption during blocking from misuse when not previously loaded.

Virtual APIC mode refresh is a running-context hook that does nothing without kernel LAPIC support or acceleration enabled, otherwise restores format-derived state and activates virtualization when active or deactivates it when not, marking control state dirty. Execution-control refresh builds on it and then loads or unloads placement with activation semantics, expecting a non-blocking caller.

Acceleration enablement follows an init-time policy where automatic mode requires extended virtualization support plus a recent processor family, explicit enablement also requires nested paging, base feature presence unless forced, and absence of a confidential platform without hypervisor-write permission. Forced enablement without feature indication and extended support without base support emit warnings.

Hardware setup resolves the enablement policy, announces activation, selects a maximum virtual processor limit for extended mode based on further capability or otherwise permits acceleration in extended addressing without virtualization, disables IPI virtualization on affected families, and registers a guest-address log notifier. Teardown unregisters that notifier when enabled.

Family identifiers 0x17 and 0x18 select processors where IPI virtualization is disabled, and value 0x1A serves as the lower bound for treating automatic-mode processors as recent enough when combined with extended support. Invalid host placement is represented by -1 during unload and affinity propagation.

Synthetic exit after TLB flush provides an operation that programs a reserved software exit code asserted equal to the Hyper-V defined value, sets trap-after-flush detail with cleared secondary detail, and then performs a nested exit.

Nested exit moves a processor from guest execution back to host control with failure containment. Update or address-load failures request triple fault rather than aborting, guest mode is left, performance and bus-lock tracking are reconciled, nested control state is cleared, runnable state is restored, and execution resumes from saved host control and register state with root address translation reinstated.

On nested exit the implementation guarantees interrupt and timing coherence: an event re-evaluation is requested when the outer guest does not intercept interrupts, branch-record state is reconciled according to outer virtualization control, virtual NMI blocking and pending indications are transferred, global interrupt flag is cleared with exit detail reset, time offset and scaling are restored to outer values, and debug single-step generates a pending exception.

Nested transition TLB handling combines a Hyper-V specific flush step honoring nested paging state with unconditional requests for MMU synchronization and current-context flush, documented as intentionally conservative pending finer-grained handling of remote, identifier and pending-flush cases.

Nested address-space loading validates control-register legality, handles extended paging structures differently by deferring reload under nested translation versus immediate load otherwise with failure on error, stores the new value, reinitializes translation to absorb mode changes, and announces a new top-level directory when not using nested translation.
Virtual branch-record support for nested control is present only when the guest exposes the corresponding capability and nested control explicitly enables virtual records.

Common control-block state shared across nesting levels is limited in this helper to speculation control, with other persistent processor state documented as always accessed via the primary control block.
Nested MMU teardown restores the architectural translation pointer to the root context, discarding the nested view without further synchronization in this helper.

Misuse and overflow hazards are contained with warnings and safe fallbacks: absent remapping metadata reverts to legacy mode, oversized host identifiers or out-of-range table indexes abort placement updates, unload without prior load warns unless blocking explains it, and execution-control toggling while blocking warns.

After acceleration state restoration the implementation refreshes destination-format and location-derived programming before reactivation, ensuring updates made while virtualization was temporarily inactive are reflected in the logical targeting tables.
